cases.answer: The AF-management review reports 12-month freedom from AF of 89% with AI-guided dispersion ablation plus PVI versus 67% with PVI alone in persistent AF. The primary TAILORED-AF trial reports 88% versus 70%, respectively, in its modified-intention-to-treat population of 357 patients. Its primary endpoint was freedom from documented AF at 12 months after a single procedure, with or without antiarrhythmic drugs. Represent these as discrepant source-specific reports: the review implies a 22-percentage-point difference, while the primary trial reports an 18-percentage-point difference. The supplied text does not establish a reason for the discrepancy; the primary trial values should be used when describing its primary results.

cases.answer: Gao's combined CCTA model predicted one-year MACE in CAD patients, with AUC 0.936 in the 280-patient derivation cohort and 0.932 in the 288-patient external validation cohort; its bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index was 0.917. Sun's combined CHA2DS2-VA model added sex, hemoglobin, platelet count, lymphocyte count, and number of implanted stents. For no-reflow in 725 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, its AUC was 0.689 overall versus 0.613 for the score alone; in males, the combined-model AUC was 0.721 versus 0.569 for the score alone. These are different prediction tasks: Gao predicts subsequent one-year cardiovascular events in CAD, whereas Sun predicts angiographic no-reflow persisting after primary PCI for STEMI. Their AUCs therefore describe discrimination for different populations, outcomes, and time points.

cases.answer: The TyG/CAD-RADS study defined MACE as myocardial infarction, all-cause mortality, and stroke. Its median follow-up was 50.4 months (IQR 39.4–55.1), with time measured from coronary CTA to MACE or the follow-up deadline. Gao's CCTA nomogram study instead defined MACE as cardiac death including fatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal myocardial infarction, coronary revascularization for unstable angina, and rehospitalization attributable to unstable angina. Gao evaluated one-year MACE, starting at the first coronary CCTA, with monthly assessments until the first event within one year or the prespecified termination date of December 31, 2023. Thus the TyG study includes stroke and all-cause death, while Gao's definition includes unstable-angina interventions and admissions and specifies cardiac death; their follow-up horizons also differ.
